correctness.rationale: Exact conditional-independence reduction proves the cumulant is the product of two nonzero covariances times (1-2p_j)/Var(X_j); hard-core Markov transitions fix covariance signs. Deletion recursion yields exact p_j odds; characteristic roots translate positive fugacity to x in (0,1). For odd n, both parity cases are settled by positive monotone factors. For even n, the paired-cosh decomposition yields strict monotonicity of S from zero to b-j and gives precisely the stated geometric cutoffs. Crossings are transversal and unique. Exact-rational independent configuration enumeration checked 1,650 triples and 306 odds identities; no finite test is used as proof of the universal claim.

originality.rationale: A fresh statement-level comparison found no covering all-length parity-and-middle-site classification in examined sources. The standard 1D Gibbs Markov property and independent-set recurrence are prior ingredients, not the novelty. Scott–Sokal study general partition functions, zeros and local-lemma bounds; Cheong–Henley work in a quantum fixed-number ground-state setting; the 1986 correlation paper investigates two-point functions at a fixed density. Closest indexed exact canonical hard-core pair covariance thresholds and separate tree/cycle third-cumulant results do not logically imply the grand-canonical open-path unique transition criterion. The complete positive-activity phase portrait remains a potentially elementary consequence of older formulas; unindexed publication priority is a residual risk.

value.rationale: The nontrivial new mathematical object is the full third connected occupancy response (Ursell function) of the classical hard-core path, not a rewritten two-point or normalization identity. The all-size phase portrait gives necessary and sufficient parity and boundary-position conditions for a genuine sign reversal, proves every occurring transition is unique and simple, counts precisely all affected triples, and identifies the sharp five-site onset. It is a complete natural response classification with finite-boundary physical meaning; higher-order functions or thermodynamic criticality are not claimed.
